note: MAPPING: code derivation pattern 1 -- data/degirolamo_2022_covid_wellbeing.py keeps the source CSV column names pag20_4_1..10 as item codes (no rename, no positional step, no reverse-coding; resp stored as deposited 1-7, wave 4 only, N=2,500). Each column's own Italian variable label in Wave4_DICTIONARY.xls reads '<adjective pair> (<shared stem>)', e.g. pag20_4_6 = 'Riservata, silenziosa (Per favore, legga ...'; the adjective pair -> item_text, verbatim, 10/10; value labels 1..7 (identical for all 10 items) -> option_text, verbatim, straight apostrophes kept as in the file. TRUNCATION: all 10 variable labels are exactly at the SPSS label cap (256 characters as read), so every label is cut inside the parenthesised stem; the adjective pairs before ' (' are intact (10/10 identical to Chiorri's I-TIPI form). instructions = the longest surviving stem prefix, which all 10 labels agree on, ending mid-word at "...Nel rispondere, consideri l'insieme delle due caratteristic" -- shipped as the literal prefix, not completed: the deposit (four wave dictionaries, English WHO template codebook, data CSVs), the paper and its supplement hold no fuller copy, and the study's stem is its own formal-Lei rewording, not Chiorri's form ('Per favore, leggi ... indica quanto ti senti descritto da ogni coppia, anche se pensi che una delle due caratteristiche ti descriva più dell'altra ...'), so Chiorri's text cannot fill the gap. Chiorri's 'Sono una persona...' lead-in is not in the deposit and was not added. Step 3b: live table is 10 items x resp 1-7, each item n=2500 with all 7 levels used; the 10 Italian pairs and the 7 anchors (Completamente in disaccordo .. Completamente d'accordo) match Chiorri's revised I-TIPI-R word for word, so the instrument is the I-TIPI-R, not Carlisle's Italian TIPI (also on Gosling's page, different wording). Informational sanity check from Valide_DATA_4W.csv (no Redivis export): item means 3.97/3.42/5.03/3.84/4.72/4.46/4.92/3.12/4.55/4.47; the three undesirable-content items 2 (polemica), 4 (ansiosa), 8 (disorganizzata) intercorrelate +0.29..+0.38 and have the lowest means after item 1, consistent with content; TIPI pair correlations are weak (E 1/6 -0.10, A 2/7 -0.01, C 3/8 -0.19, ES 4/9 -0.13, O 5/10 +0.24), a known TIPI property that does not bear on the code mapping. ENGLISH (translation_source=mixed): item_text_translated for items 1,2,3,4,6,7,9 is Gosling et al.'s (2003) official English (tipi.pdf), trailing periods dropped; items 5, 8 and 10 are Chiorri's REVISED wordings ('con molti interessi', 'distratta', 'Tradizionalista, abitudinaria') that Gosling's 'complex', 'careless', 'Conventional, uncreative' do not translate, so those three and instructions_translated and option_text_translated are this project's own English (machine_translation class) -- an issues-page entry is owed on upload. instructions_translated mirrors the source truncation. RIGHTS: originator Gosling's TIPI page: 'WANT TO USE THE TIPI? GO AHEAD. ANYONE CAN USE IT FOR ANY PURPOSE. NO NEED TO ASK ME FOR PERMISSION.' On translations the same page says 'As far as I know, you are free to use these translations but as a courtesy I encourage you to contact the contact persons listed below before doing so.' -- a courtesy request, not a reserved right; Chiorri's I-TIPI.doc states no terms. Same page and sha256 as batch_454 celik_2026_tipi and batch_455 gcbs_brotherton_2013_tipi. The Italian wording itself came from the CC BY 4.0 deposit. instrument_rights_register.csv has no TIPI row; none written (rounds may not write ship rows) -- escalated as ship-shaped with the quotes above.
public_note: Item and response wording is the Italian revised Ten-Item Personality Inventory (I-TIPI-R) as administered; the instructions are cut off mid-word because the source codebook truncates them, English for items 5, 8 and 10 (revised in the Italian form), the instructions and the response labels was translated by IRW, and the other seven English items are Gosling et al.'s original wording.

note: Code derivation: pattern 1 -- data/modzelewska_2021_interoception.py melts the .sav columns Emo_neg_aut1-5 and Emo_neg_ref1-5 under their own names, no rename. Mapping: the s001.sav VARIABLE labels give the English word per code, 10/10 (Emo_neg_aut1=Suffering, aut2=Helplessness, aut3=Frustration, aut4=Breakdown, aut5=Terror, ref1=Shame, ref2=Sadness, ref3=Dejection, ref4=Depression, ref5=Envy); this agrees 10/10 with the order of the s004 questionnaire list and with the paper's automatic/reflective lists. Value labels are bare '1'..'7' (no anchors). Language: administered Polish (Qualtrics; s004 is titled an English translation). item_text = the Polish word as printed in the paper's Methods 'Types of emotions' (e.g. 'Suffering (Polish: Cierpienie)'), item_text_translated = the study's English (s004 / .sav labels, identical). The Polish instruction sentence and Polish anchors are NOT recoverable: checked the paper full text, s001.sav (labels in English only), s002.docx (appendix, English), s003.pdf (the English MAIA form, 0 Polish diacritics), s004.docx (English translation) -- so instructions and the two endpoint anchors ship the study's s004 English in the BASE fields with the _translated twins empty (fallback for those fields only), hence text_source=translated_substitute; all English is the study's own, so translation_source=study_supplied. Anchors: s004 labels only 1 'to a small extent' and 7 'to a significant extent'; points 2-6 left blank. Lowercase as printed in s004's quotes. Rights: study-authored list of single emotion words (selected on Imbir 2016's automatic/reflective distinction, no upstream instrument); first published in a CC BY 4.0 article; no restriction found to quote. Silence -> ships; no register row written. Live data: 10 items x 299, resp 1..7 all used on every item (irw_table_sets per_item). validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (first attempt hung >15 min on the Redivis query and was killed; retry passed in <5 min).
public_note: Item wording is the Polish emotion word respondents rated, with English alongside, but the instruction sentence and the two endpoint anchors are the study's English translation because the Polish questionnaire text was not published.
